utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, there's a notable absentee this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, my colleague Mr. Lukic had a medical issue that required urgent intervention, for which he will not be with us at least for today and probably not for the next couple days as well, as the situation develops. I have been in contact with him and have spent the weekend preparing and therefore could continue in his place with the cross of this witness, if that pleases the Court and with the Court's leave, I believe, since I don't know the procedural aspects at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, not only does it please the Court, we're grateful to you for taking on that responsibility, Mr. Ivetic, and we would ask you to extend our wishes to Mr. Lukic for a speedy recovery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jelic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a change in personnel in court today because of the illness of Mr. Lukic, who was cross-examining you. That further cross-examination will be conducted by Mr. Ivetic who was speaking a moment ago. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you gave at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, General. As you know, my name is Dan Ivetic, one difference is that I will have to do my cross-examination in English, so please if one of my questions is unclear to you, please ask me and I will try to either rephrase it or repeat it so that you get the proper translation and so that we get to the truth of the matter and conclude your testimony in the most efficient way possible. Now, first of all, sir, I would like to touch on some areas from your testimony the other days. First of all, with respect to the border belt, would you agree with me that the police is only situated at the 50 metres surrounding the official border crossing and is not present in the remainder of the border belt, which would be controlled and patrolled by the border troops of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the police was at the border crossing in its sector, which would be about 50 to 100 metres, and outside of that area the whole of the border was kept secure by the army. The border battalions and the in-depth security units secured the whole border facing the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask you some questions about the military territorial detachments or the VTO. With respect to the VTO, how many VTO were to be found within your zone of authority in 1999 and which specific detachments were these?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to decision of the Pristina Corps commander, I was assigned two territorial detachments in the first stage and later on a third one, that was the Vitina detachment, Urosevac detachment, and Strpce detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the sake of detail, you mentioned the Vitina, Urosevac, and Strpce Detachments. Are we talking about the 60th, the 64th, and the 66th VTO detachments?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, these are the detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when were these VTOs actually mobilised, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These detachments were mobilised by the military district. We did not mobilise them. It was their superior command who issued this order to them and they carried out the mobilisation. Once the mobilisation was done, they were resubordinated to the brigade command. They were mobilised before and during the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say "before and during the aggression," am I to understand you that the mobilisation started occurring in March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in late March, on the eve of the aggression, and right at the very start of the aggression, or rather, the air-strike campaign.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go back to a topic that my friend and colleague Mr. Lukic started with you on Friday at the end of the day. Specifically you were called -- you were asked about Kotlina, and first of all during the examination of my friend and colleague Mr. Cepic at page 18906, lines 2 through 5 of the transcript, you stated that the VJ forces were 1.5 kilometres from the villages of Kotlina and Ivaja then at 18907 lines 2 through 8 you said the army never entered these villages and you further reiterated this position at transcript page 18908, lines 25 through 18909 line 10 emphatically stating that the army could not carry out manoeuvres on the day in question, which I believe was the 23rd, 24th of March 1999. Now the first question I want to ask you about is you as the commanding officer for the VJs of the 243rd Motorised Brigade issued any order or planned any action on the part of either VJ or MUP units to blockade, rout and eliminate the Siptar terrorist forces in the region of Kotlina to be executed on 23 March 1999.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you made a couple of claims here that I'm supposed to confirm. The first positions were located 1 kilometre -- 1 and a half kilometres to 2 kilometres away from the village. Those positions were under constant threat and the unit was in constant engagement because this was actually in the border belt. If I understood you right, in the time-period that you're referring to, I already stated that on the 23rd and the 24th we came under very intense attack right there at the Golimo Brdo and Belo Brdo hills. The terrorist forces launched a fierce attack on the positions of Combat Group 3. The strength of Combat Group 3 in accordance with the agreement was about one company. Those were the units that were carrying out the in-depth securing of the state border in addition to the border battalion which carried out the line security of the border. The unit never entered the village, and it fought to the south and to the west against the terrorists from the village of Kotlina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, General. And again, as a commanding officer of the VJ's 243rd Motorised Brigade, did you issue any order, or "zapovest," or planned any action on the part of either the VJ or the MUP to blockade, rout, and eliminate the Siptar terrorist forces in the region of Kotlina, to be executed on 23 March 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as in all the areas, we had plans in place for counter-terrorist actions. And in this area an action had been planned to block, rout, and destroy the terrorist forces, because according to the data that we had they depended -- depending on the source, the size of the terrorist organization was between 200 and 600 terrorists in the Kotlina area. Our plan was to block, rout, and destroy this terrorist organization, together with MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- the plan was to carry this out on the 21st or the 22nd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, you might recall that the last question or series of questions asked by my colleague on Friday at transcript page 18689 lines 18 to 23 was about the existence of a "zapovest" dated the 21st of March, 1999, where -- and in your response you denied recollection of such a document. I'd like to call up 6D145 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, that document is not on the list of the documents of the 6D Defence, it was not on their list and it is not in e-court at all. It was not announced that it would be used with this witness. So this is a document that in my humble opinion is not relevant enough to be put to this witness, in light of these procedural deficiencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Relevance is a separate matter from whether the failure to comply with procedure is a basis for rejecting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if counsel is finished --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Procedural, procedural, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the number was 1465, is that right, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 1465. It should be in e-court. It was e-mailed to the parties on Friday as an attachment with the document as soon as this witness is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I gather it is there, Mr. Cepic. Now, what is your response, Mr. Ivetic, to the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The response is, Your Honours, that the 65 ter summary announcing this summary for this witness filed on the 8th of November, 2007, did not give any indication that this witness was going to depart from or change his testimony from the Milosevic proceedings. There was no notice that -- and we were quite shocked to find the army denying entry into Kotlina at the testimony on Friday. We immediately turned to the documents that we thought would be quite known to the army, since they were disclosed to the 5D Defence, and in fact if we go into this document we'll see why I think the witness ought to know about the document. So we were quite shocked to find this testimony come out on Friday, quite disturbed by it, and we have to defend against it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's sufficient for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's perfectly understandable to us why this document was not notified. It's plainly relevant to the issues being explored, and therefore we will allow you to continue with the examination on this issue, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, I apologise for the interruption. We have 6D1465 on the screen. For -- before I burden you with questions about this document, I'd like to go to the last page of the same so we can see why I think it's relevant to you and why I think you have knowledge of the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a translation of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, this document was not intended to be introduced into evidence by us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Since we thought this was an issue that would not be contested by the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have, I think, submitted it, but obviously CLSS takes three days. I didn't try to give them anything over night so there's no chance it's been translated already.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General Jelic, if you look at the lower right-hand corner of this document that's on the screen, would you confirm for us whether, in fact, the signature and stamp on this document belong to yourself and the command of the 243rd Motorised Brigade of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see here that this is my stamp and my full name and my signature, but the stamp is really not all that legible. I assume that it comes from my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can now return to the first page, I want to see if you have any recollection of the subject matter of this document. You'll see there the title [Interpretation] "Order for the blockade, routing, and destruction of STC in the broader region of Kotlina." [In English] Do you recall issuing such an order on or about the 21st of March, 1999, bearing the strictly confidential number 400-290?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that it comes from the brigade command and that it has this -- bears this number, but I will have to read it to acquaint myself with the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the delay. I'm waiting for the translation and transcript into English to catch up with us. Well, let me ask you this first: Was the log-book number 400 in fact kept by your brigade during March of 1999 and would that number apply to a "zapovest" for an anti- terrorist action to be conducted by units under your command?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this number is the brigade number. It doesn't necessarily mean that an anti-terrorist would be carried out; it is a number that is assigned by the superior command and all other orders and reports that go to the brigade carry the same number. So this is the number that was used from the 23rd of March until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify, General, would "zapovesti" or orders for anti-terrorist actions be recorded under that number in the log-book of the command of the 243rd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the documents, including this order, were recorded in the brigade registry book and the first number would always be 400, that was the basic number, and then all the other numbers would follow in sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, I apologise, I was waiting for the transcript to catch up with us to make the job of the court staff easier. Now, you indicated you would like to look at the subject matter of the document. I direct your attention to section 4, which is three-quarters of the way down on the first page, "odluka" is the Serbian title or "decision" in English. And I would direct your attention to the first line there and I would ask you to read that first line which starts with "odlucio sam" and tell me whether that refreshes your recollection as to whether you planned an action for execution in Kotlina for the night of the 23rd/24th March 1999 in which both VJ and MUP forces were to be employed.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I have decided to carry out the bringing in and deployment of the forces in the light between the 23rd and 24th of March, 1999, to block the area Bojevo-Globocica road, Belo Brdo, trig point 1028; Golimo Brdo, trig point 986; Ruksu-Foelne-Maja e Solanit-Djeneral Jankovic-Kacanik road, and from the line Mali Tupan-Buzovik-Gurikec launch an attack grouping the main force along the axis Mali Tupan-village of Kotlina- and the auxiliary force along the axis Gurikec-Ivaja Pustenik. "Objective: Block the broader area in order to prevent the ex-filtration of the Siptar terrorist forces, rout and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces using some elements of the force and establish the control of the territory and roads as follows: Globocica, village of Doganovic and Djeneral Jankovic, Kacanik."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I think the transcript's caught up with us now. And again, I ask you, does this refresh your recollection that you drafted and planned for an action to be undertaken on the 23rd/24th of March, 1999, by VJ and MUP forces, a legitimate anti-terrorist action against the strong Albanian terrorist forces located in Kotlina village?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my decision, planning the destruction of the Siptar terrorist forces in the broader region of Kotlina and Ivaja within the border belt, that would be 3 to 4 kilometres from the Macedonian border.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, if we can stay in that section you see there the next section which I believe translates "borbeni raspored," which I believe translates to battle order. There are multiple types of forces listed there, and since I don't have a translation I would ask you to read out the various forces and I will ask you about the last item on that page before we move on. Which forces were envisioned under this battle order for your action in Kotlina village for the 23rd/24th March 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The combat disposition for the routing and destruction of the Siptar terrorist forces, the forces for the blocking, support forces, road repair group, reserve force, rear support forces, and command and communication forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, the last item is forces for communication and command, and if we turn to the next page of this exhibit at the top of the page it, in fact, mentions that the KM of the 243rd mbr in the region of Djeneral Jankovic is referenced there. Does that apply to the forces for command and communications of this operation and was that, in fact, the command post for your unit at Djeneral Jankovic on about the 23rd/24th March 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This pertains to the command post that was planned for counter-terrorist combat. The brigade command post was never in Djeneral Jankovic because this is situated at the very border, less than a kilometre from the border crossing, it's in a military facility that -- that was actually a depot that used to belong to RVO and later it was assigned to my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, on this page we have section 5, assignments to the units, and at section 5.1 there at the top of the page we see assignments for various units and I'd like to ask you first, in 5.1, all of these units listed are VJ units; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are all the units of the Army of Yugoslavia. There are no other units under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, would you be so kind as to read for us the section in 5.1 pertaining to the main forces, exactly as written, because we've had much testimony about what the meanings of "sadejstva" or joint combat are. Could you tell us what the main forces of this VJ component were tasked with doing in this "zapovest," decision, as well as the secondary or "pomocne snage."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The task for the main force in concerted action with the PJP platoon, to rout and destroy the forces on the axis village of Straza, village of Ivaja, Mahala next to the "dzamija," that's next to the mosque and the auxiliary forces in concerted action with the platoon of the PJP rout and destroy the forces on the axis of Kotlinska Reka, village of Kotlina, and ensure the control of the territory, command post in the sector of the village of Straza 500 metres to the north."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, I see it's been recorded in the transcript the KM was recorded as command post. Is that correct, that KM is an abbreviation for command post and that this command post in the village was one familiar to you because it was a command post of one of your subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "KM" means command post. It was planned to be in Straza village.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we can look at section 5.3, that starts off "VOD SAJ i IO." First of all, who are or what is the VOD SAJ or IO in this context? These are army units, are they not?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, you're wrong there. SAJ platoon is a police unit, and IO means reconnaissance squad. They are to take up and hold position on the line, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct, General, but I believe you told me some time ago or a couple of moments ago that only army units were under your command, but here in 5.3 you've identified that the SAJ is a police unit that is the subject of your orders. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My units receive orders from me, and since there was no resubordination, despite the fact that I wrote the order, I had to cover in my order all the units in order to avoid accidents and friendly fire, but as you know these other units were never actually resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether I know that, but my knowledge is not at issue here, General. You've mentioned the reconnaissance squad, the IO. You failed to mention what formation that was a part of. Was that a police formation or was it a VJ formation, General?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reconnaissance squad is part of the army, that's combat armoured vehicle manned by three persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And isn't the task of a reconnaissance squad to move forward from the main units?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahead of main units, he cannot go reconnoitring from the personnel carrier. He can act from a cover, from shelter, and go forward in leaps to detect the enemy. Because an armoured personnel carrier, without support, is not a carrier, he's a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, General, in your order here at 5.3 isn't it a fact that the assignment given is to rout and eliminate terrorist forces in Kotlina with the secondary forces securing the right flank of the main forces. Surely your reconnaissance squad was not the one securing the flank, but rather was leaping forward, as you indicated, under the support of this SAJ unit you've indicated. Isn't that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this reconnaissance squad provides support to the SAJ platoon, that is allowed. If you take into account the balance of forces, the platoon is supported by one armoured carrier, in this case it's reconnoitring vehicle, that's according to the rules of use of combat equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And they move forward together; isn't that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, when they move, they move forward but not necessarily together. One supports the platoon. It -- it's about providing support in the best-case scenario up to the line. Generally support is always located behind, and you can see that from the rule, from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm having a little bit of difficulty, perhaps you can help me. My Serbian might not be as good. Where do you see the word "podrska" in 5.3. I see "Razbiti i unistiti snage na pravcu," which to me means something different.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the task, whereas the mode of movement is what I'm trying to explain. The carrier can go alone manned by three men, 300 or 400 metres ahead of the combat formation because that would be certain death. They are usually on the line and sometimes behind the line. They move forward in leaps from cover to cover and from a safe place conduct reconnaissance. I'm speaking of regular reconnaissance, not force reconnaissance which is a completely different action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But he's surely not alone. He's with that -- that unit is with the VOD of the SAJ, which you said was a police unit. Could you tell us a little bit more about this police unit that is in your "zapovest." Who exactly are they?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of coordinated action, a plan has been made with the MUP about the way to crush terrorist forces in this area. I don't know the strength of that unit and it's not I who determine it; it's determined by its own superior, in this case the chief of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, General, if the SAJ is the SAJ we've heard evidence about here in this courtroom, surely this is a special anti-terrorist police unit and not a police unit from the SUP or secretariat of internal affairs, as you have just identified.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that unit does not go through the Army of Yugoslavia, it's not resubordinated to me via the corps command or via brigades; it is resubordinated by the command of the SUP. I don't even know them until they get in touch through the liaison officer from the SUP. I don't even know who they consist of or their strength.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at 5.4, the next paragraph, we see there that a CPJP, which I believe is a short form for a "ceta" or detachment of the PJP with again the IO having a similar assignment on the other side of Kotlina, and I would ask you: Do you allow for the possibility that the decision VOD SAJ in 5.3 is a typographical error, and that in fact we're talking about two detachments of the PJP, who in fact would be through the SUP the "ceta," or units I guess is the English translation for "ceta."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it's a typographical error. Those were the units that we received. We got certain information about them, and on that basis we issued tasks. I don't know why it would be a typographical error. A unit is identified, it is enumerated along with the others, and once we get information about what we dispose of, tasks are issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We -- we see here you say that based upon this information tasks are issued. What tasks did you issue to the "ceta" of the PJP and the IO in 5.4 for this action for Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written here. Do you want me to read it? Because it's quite legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If that helps you, sir, yes, that's fine. What's the assignment given to these main forces, which I assume would be the PJP, what assignments of tasks did you give to the PJP in section 5.4 of your order?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Take control of the line Lepenac trig point 914 (to the north-west by 1.000). Task: Use main forces to rout and destroy Siptar terrorist forces along the axis: Trig point 560, Gajre village, trip point 887; Ivaja village, and use auxiliary forces along the axis: Mil trig point 914; village Ivaja, crush sabotage terrorist forces, secure the right flank of the main forces, and take control of the territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Microphone again, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, if we look down the page to paragraph 5.8, and I believe this relates to the same PJP units, and could you read just that first sentence and then I would like to ask you if, in fact, this confirms that both the PJP and battle group 3 were involved in a concerted action, a concerted attack pursuant to a legitimate anti-terrorist action planned by this order.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a platoon of MB, that is, mortar 120-millimetres from the composition of Combat Group 3. I did not understand your second question. What is the second part of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me simplify this for you. According to my reading of 5.8, battle group 3 is to support the attack of the joint forces upon a request of either the commander of BG 3 or the commander of the PJP. And so the question I have for you is: Can -- is it obvious or can we conclude from this that both BG 3 and the PJP were engaged in a concerted attack against legitimate targets, namely, the terrorists that were in Kotlina village? Because surely the commander of the BG 3 would not be requesting -- requesting support for units not under his command. So I'm assuming that the commander for BG 3 would be requesting support for his units from the 120-millimetre guns that are listed in this paragraph. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that it was planned, not that it participated. It's correct that this task was planned with the support of this mortar platoon at the request of the commander of Combat Group 3 and the CO of the PJP company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say it's correct that it was planned but not participated. Are you denying the existence of a post-combat report for this very same action signed by yourself for the 243rd Motorised Brigade dated the 24th of March, 1999, strictly confidential number 400-302. General, wasn't it, in fact, the legitimate anti-terrorist action in Kotlina carried out by both VJ and MUP forces in accordance with your "zapovest" that we've gone through here now?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several questions are included in fact in your question, and they are in fact assertions rather than questions. This is a planning document made in various units, covering various units, for the purpose of performing this task. All the units are identified, and based on their abilities a plan is made. The execution of a plan is something entirely different. We didn't read this through to the end because in order to understand an order it must be read in its entirety. I would not wish now to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question isn't about the order. The question you're being asked now is whether a legitimate anti-terrorist action was carried -- was actually carried out by both VJ and MUP forces in accordance with the decision. Now, what's the answer to that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this anti-terrorist action, it was indeed legitimate, was performed by MUP units and VJ units in a planned manner, but not according to this plan. If you want me, I can explain, because the critical period from the 21st to the 24th was critical for the whole of Army of Yugoslavia, but especially for my brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ivetic will want to clarify that. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The question I have for you, sir, is: According to my information - and my information is based on the post-combat report signed by you, strictly confidential number 400-302 - is that you reported that in carrying out this action the VJ and MUP forces killed 26 terrorists. Now, to me, that means that either your own VJ forces participated in the attack, the legitimate attack, and entered Kotlina to fight with the terrorists, or that the subordinated MUP units under your command participating in the action reported to you the various details of their struggle with the terrorist forces. Which of these or both are true?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of the options you named. The army participated, that's a fact, in the anti-terrorist action to destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in Kotlina with the support -- in the support of MUP forces in order to take certain features. The MUP forces entered the village, checked identity papers of the population, and searched the village. The army did not enter; that is strictly prohibited by several orders from several levels, including the corps. It is strictly prohibited for the army to enter populated areas and come into contact with the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have two questions. Your statement that it's strictly prohibited for the VJ to enter any built-up or populated area, does that also apply to areas -- specifically apply to areas within the border belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, within the border belt as well the army was prohibited from entering houses and populated areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the second question, your answer earlier to me was that the action was carried out but not in accordance with this particular order. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I meant to say the following: This was a planned task that resulted from a period of the army suffering losses over a time, so in concerted action with the MUP an anti-terrorist action was planned in this volume. Since from the 21st to the 24th the corps commander made his own mobilisation plan, ordering that mobilisation should be conducted and units should leave barracks. Therefore, on the 22nd and the 23rd a new situation arose. All units had to be pulled out of barracks. You have to bear in mind that there were only three combat groups outside of barracks, and they were one company strong. The -- all of the other units were in barracks. In those 48 hours we had to pull out the entire brigade from barracks to make a map according to the corps commander's decision, and to organize the firing system so that the units planned for this action were considerably reduced because Combat Group 3 had to be built-up to battalion level now that it was in the first defence belt right next to the border. It was the critical time for attack. We have to bear in mind they had to pull out in just a few days thousands of tonnes of ammunition and equipment out of barracks, because already on the 25th their barracks were razed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't need a history of the war for this. Is there another document that intervenes, another order or decision before the action was carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment, I don't have that paper with me. I remember I reduced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was there one at the time that changed the identity of the task or the units or groups that were to undertake the task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There certainly is an order with a brigade for the given period and the units that were to perform this task were reduced. This reduction of forces was stipulated by my order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And thank you, General. You started answering one of

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY'S QUESTIONS BY SAYING
utterances.text: "I remember I reduced," is it your testimony that this action that was carried out was carried out in accordance with a plan that you prepared, whether it was in a shortened decision form or a "zapovest" form is irrelevant. But was the operation carried out in accordance with instructions and tasks as you planned them for units, including VJ and MUP?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That anti-terrorist action was performed with new equipment, new forces in a different way. It was not possible to execute it with the reduced forces we had over a same area with the same tasks, because if you reduce forces down to the level of a reinforced company then that same task is no longer possible. So the task was new and the forces were new; however, the objective was attained.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the execution of this objective in a different way was undertaken pursuant to a plan that you as the VJ commander on the ground gave to the units in the field. Isn't that correct? You planned the action that was undertaken and the tasks to be carried out therein?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I planned tasks for my units, I gave them excerpts from the order and the map, based on which they did their own planning documents. The plans for MUP were made by their superiors, I suppose the secretariat in Urosevac or maybe Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to show the witness the document that I'd tried to ask questions about because I don't have it in the system, because again after -- after seeing a "zapovest" for the action, I didn't think that the general would then require refreshment of his recollection as to how the action was carried out. This is the combat report of the command of the 243rd Motorised Brigade that I cited to earlier. It's about a half-page document bearing a stamp and a signature, and it again is not in e-court and I would only have two questions with respect -- actually, even one question with respect to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object to this, Your Honour. We had no occasion to see this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's apparently a document of the brigade that the witness should be familiar with. Can that be a problem? Because if we don't see it, we're not going to get the full picture, are we? He seems to need assistance with his recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has not seen this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ivetic, could you please give Mr. Cepic a copy so that he can consider it before we proceed further?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know how this Defence got hold of this document and I am not sure about its authenticity. Therefore, I cannot -- rather, I do not agree that it be put to the witness for the stated reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, we will allow you to put this document to the witness, but you will have to bear in mind there's a challenge to its authenticity at the moment. So you'll have to deal with that issue first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that means I'll have more than one question for the witness on the document. If I can have the assistance of the usher, I have a copy that can be put on the ELMO so that both the witness and for the sake of the record we can have it in front of us since it's not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, General, if you could first look at the bottom of the document. Mr. Cepic has questioned the authenticity of the document. Is the stamp and the signature on this document familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise it, it's most probably the Chief of Staff who signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that would be Dragan Kolundzija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And his initials appear below the signature. If we look at the top of the document, the source is listed as the command of the 243rd Motorised Brigade [Interpretation] "Confidential number 400-302" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, let's start that all over again in English, please, otherwise the transcript will go awry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, am I correct that the top of the document indicates, first in handwritten form: "Strictly confidential number 400-302," underneath it "command of the 243rd Motorised Brigade," then typewritten: "Strictly confidential 400-302," with the date 24th March 1999. Is this the format and indeed official document of the command of the 243rd Motorised Brigade of which you were the commanding officer in March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In formal and legal terms, it's illegal to have the same number noted down twice in the heading, so the handwritten bit has been added on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, General, the "zapovest" that you said was yours also had the handwritten number in the left corner with the typewritten number. Was that one also done improperly or illegally?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In formal and legal terms, wherever it appears, that's incorrect. It's correct only when it says "strictly confidential number 400," regardless of whether it's handwritten or typewritten, through such-and-such a number. But this is written twice over. Probably this was done before archiving in order to make it more legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you're not challenging the fact that this document actually originated from your command, are you?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't challenge this, I see no reason. This is a copy. If it's stamped, you can't really see the stamp very well in the lower right-hand corner, it's probably authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to combat reports of your unit that were sent out, was it the regular custom and practice to have the Chief of Staff of your command send documents out on your behalf; and if so, would you still have knowledge of the matters contained in such reports and wouldn't that be your duty as the commander?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff in my brigade was also my deputy with all the rights and powers that I had if I was absent. In view of the time here, that this was the critical time when the mobilisation of the brigade was carried out. It was the Chief of Staff who signed this document, and it's quite normal for him to have sent it to the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would it be quite normal and indeed required for you to also be apprised of the contents of such a report sent by your Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Certainly I would have been apprised of the contents of such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd like to direct your attention to section 2, and I think just for the sake of giving you the full picture so that I don't read anything out of context, if you could read the entirety of section 2, both paragraphs, and then I'll ask you my question that I had with respect to this document and whether it refreshes your recollection of the events post the operation, the legitimate operation in Kotlina against the terrorist forces located therein.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Part of the forces of Combat Group 3 (6 OTM-60, 3 BVP M-80, 4 BRDH-2, and 2 spat 30/2-millimetre Praga) with part of the forces of the 57," --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Jelic, the interpreter did not pick up which battalion you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The 57 Border Battalion, Combat Group-21/NK, two companies of the PJP carried out a blockade of the general area where the Siptar terrorist forces are concentrated. Through characteristic activities the Siptar terrorist forces were routed and the 26 terrorists were liquidated, about 20 barrels of weapons were captured, and in the course of the activities a group of mines was demined, four anti-tank mines, and an auxiliary device with a lighter envisaged to activate this by radio was demined -- the fuses were demined."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. That's the first paragraph. I can ask you a question with respect to that. First of all, do you see in section 1 there the village of Kotlina is identified as the locale, that's the villages of Straza and Kotlina, Straza being the place that the "zapovest" envisioned as being the command centre in Kotlina being the village that we have been discussing as being the locale for this action. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see that anywhere that Straza is the command post. I don't know where this is supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it was a translation error. Does item 1 of this post-combat report of your unit indicate that the actions being reported were being undertaken in the region of the village of Straza and the village of Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that activities were manifested in the area of the villages of Straza and Kotlina on the Bojevo-Globocica axis, that's from Kotlina 2 kilometres to the west and then to the south towards Duganovic and Globocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so, General, in section 2 when you recited those various VJ forces and the two PJP units, they all were in the same region, performing the same task; isn't that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the general task assigned to the units, to block, rout -- block and rout these terrorist forces on the areas -- in the areas of Slatina, Kotlina, Bojevo, up to the border crossing at Globocica. That's a wide area, a broad area, 3 to 4 kilometres in diameter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I see here that there's two "ceta" of the PJP. Was one of the changes that you made to the actual action that was carried out from the "zapovest" to not involve the SAJ because they were not taking part in the actual action that took place? That is to say, does this document refresh your recollection as to whether, in fact, the SAJ did not take part in this action, that it was two "ceta" from the PJP of Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here there were two PJP companies, whether the SAJ was there or not, I can't recall. The units enumerated here were mostly involved in the blockade, even my 57th Border Battalion which did not participate in the activities but because it was there, it was engaged in blocking that unit probably, and what you have just said may be a technical error and may have been omitted from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this very detailed knowledge of the number of terrorists killed, the number of long-barrelled weapons recovered, the discovery of mines and trenches in villages, if you had gone on to read the second paragraph where you stopped, either you received very detailed information from your units that were in the midst of this all or you received information from the MUP units that were carrying out your tasks or perhaps both. Would you concede that, General, that's the only way you could have had such detailed information to present in your post-combat report?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your statement is not correct. The MUP forces were not carrying out my tasks, as you said. I reject that. There was the chief of the SUP, who issued them with tasks. All the weapons found in the villages, when we learned about that from the units we were supporting and with which we were engaged in coordinated action, just as the MUP sent information to their staff, we probably sent -- we sent information to our command. And all the equipment that was found was to be on a common list, a joint list, and had to correspond. Whatever weapon we found on the ground we always informed the MUP forces, whether in this action or any other one. It doesn't make any difference. So all the weapons and equipment were reported through the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question also relates to casualties. How would you get the information about the number of casualties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of casualties is something we learned after the end of this anti-terrorist action because the MUP forces entered, the investigating judge arrived, an attempt was made to identify the corpses. As far as I can recall, they stayed until late in the evening carrying out identifications, searches, confiscating or collecting weapons, and doing everything else that was to have been done in the village and in this action. The investigating judge arrived. As far as I can remember, they took photographs, but I don't want to go into any further detail because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, after the investigative judge arrived and tried to do the investigation, isn't it a fact that the terrorist forces attacked, causing both the VJ and the MUP to retreat from Kotlina-Ivaja?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area where the army was to the east and west where the blockade was being carried out, through manoeuvres and movements, not just fire, there was no provocation from that area nor any attacks by terrorist forces because that area was very well protected. The attacks took place from the south and the east, from the mountainous part, and according to what the chief of the SUP told me, they were unable to carry out the on-sight investigation to the end because of the danger, because of the threat. This was in populated area, built-up area, and they might have been killed on the streets of that village. To what extent they managed to complete the investigation, I'm not competent to say, and that information is not available. But I do know that the chief of the SUP told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now I'd like to take a few moments to go through your testimony regarding Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We can take that exhibit down and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What are you going to do about entering this into e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to get it entered and I will obviously have a translation done and I will move the Court for admission, and in that motion I will give the source of the documentation to address all the -- any remaining issues of authenticity that may arise in the due course of when a translation is available so that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, meanwhile it will be given an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC143, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when you make your filing that will be to substitute the document in e-court with an appropriate number for that IC143.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, with respect to Kacanik town itself, you mentioned Kacanik earlier. First of all, do you recall that on the 27th of March, 1999, there was a terrorist attack upon a column of the VJ in the village of Bob, B-o-b, on which the VJ returned live fire?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall the precise date, but I do know there was more than one attack in that area from the end of March until the very last day of the air-strike campaign against the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that the attack occurred in the region of the factory in the village of Bob, B-o-b, where the VJ was located, the VJ column?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, not in a single house of the village of Bob was there a factory, nor was the VJ located there. There were almost daily attacks on the columns, not in that area but in the entire area between the roads going from Duganovici to Globocica and from Duganovici to Djeneral Jankovic. When I say the VJ, I'm not referring just to my own brigade, other units of the corps also used those roads and they suffered very fierce attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, General, if your colleague, chief Bogi Janicevic of the Urosevac SUP would report about a KLA attack on an army unit in Bob on the 27th of March, 1999, do you have any reason why you would dispute or debate such an attack happening? Why would he report information about the VJ in such a manner?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for a single moment did I challenge his sending of information or receiving information from me. I am not denying what he said, but I'm just saying I don't know what the precise date was, whether it was the 27th or the 26th. All I can say is that there was an attack on a moving column almost every other day, whether it was part of the brigade or the corps, it didn't make any difference, because on a 150-kilometre stretch there were major roads which were under constant attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you said there were attacks on moving columns. Were there attacks on moving columns of the VJ going through the village of Bob and through the town of Kacanik -- or I should say the outskirts of the town of Kacanik, since it's my understanding that Bob is precisely on the outskirts of the town of Kacanik, separated by either a stream or some other natural feature.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main road from Pristina-Kacanik-Djeneral Jankovic passes right next to the populated area of Kacanik. A VJ unit was never attacked in the town itself because it never entered the town. I exclude the possibility that it was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How about the road on the outskirts, maybe it's a translation error. The Serbian word I'm looking for is "periferija" [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the outskirts of Kacanik, on that road, there were very frequent attacks. Several officers and soldiers were killed there. I stated that during my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, General. I'd like to have you take a look at Exhibit 6D736 briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this exhibit was announced at a later stage, six or seven hours after the making of the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, according to my staff, this document was disclosed before the witness testified on Friday, that is to say, it was disclosed sometime on Thursday I believe -- it may very well have been after his examination-in-chief, I don't know, since at that time I was engaged in other tasks for the defence of my client. So I cannot be 100 per cent certain as to that. The document itself I believe arose out of some testimony that I have here, citations to some questions posed by Your Honour to the witness and the answers received therefrom. The document itself, as can be seen, as it is in e-court, is a post-combat report of the 243rd Motorised Brigade of the VJ, and if we need more information about that I can provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, you've obviously had time to consider this document. Is there some other objection to it beyond the failure to intimate it in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My main objection is that it was not notified on time; and secondly, I may be making an error, but in the e-court system it says that the document was rejected. But I'm no expert for this e-court system, so I may be wrong there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you accept that the subject matter arises out of questions which were asked by the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just have a minute to view the contents of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What we can do is we can take the break now, Mr. Cepic, and allow you to do that and then come back and resume. We'll resume at 11.00. We have to have a break now again, Mr. Jelic, so will you please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you again at 11.00. When we resume at 11.00, we will sit until 12.45, and then we'll break for an hour, and then we'll sit from 1.45 until 3.30, as we indicated on Friday was possible. We now know that that can be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We had taken the break to see about 6D736, so I don't know if we have any need for additional submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I looked through this document carefully and it does stem from my examination-in-chief. My examination-in-chief was announced as early as in June. So let me just be very specific to reply to what Mr. Ivetic said. The questions do not relate to the questions asked by Your Honours, but it -- the questions may only stem from my examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I take that as a concession of the relevance of this document to show the true picture. I have here several transcript references when the document was first raised. I had said that it was in response to a question from the Trial Chamber. Apparently counsel stated it's in response to his questions. I think the document is relevant. I think it goes to the fact that the 65 ter summary for this witness that I've referred to previously in discussions about Slatina and Dubrava does not give details indicating or tending to indicate that the VJ units did not participate in the action. In fact, it just says that he'll explain the actions. Given the existence of these documents, I believe my counsel -- my colleague Mr. Lukic surely anticipated that the VJ would admit that the legitimate actions were carried out in the manner carried out. And when Mr. Cepic led the witness to untold territory that all of a sudden now it's the MUP acting alone. That's why we needed to bring in these documents, and I think the fact that we introduced it as early as possible I think even before the Friday testimony, I think goes towards-- towards showing we have tried to comply to give notice to the other side. Indeed it is a document that is authentic and is relevant. So at the end of the day, especially with the tempo that we're working here with in these proceedings, I think that the interests of justice ought to prevail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many more examples can we anticipate this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, to be honest, having not been the one that drafted the notification, I can't tell, Your Honour, but I don't think that many since I don't have -- I have maybe -- well, let me check with my staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There was an addendum sent out of documents on Thursday evening, but I think of that addendum I'm not actually using more than maybe this document and one more from what I can see perhaps. So there will be one more, I think 6D1313 that will come up later in my cross-examination that is also subject to the same addendum that was sent out at -- on Thursday, after the witness had taken his -- had taken the oath but before he testified on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Since it is accepted that this document is relevant to issues which are -- have arisen, and since it appears to us to be important to have a view of the complete picture, and since notice was given last week of the intention to use it, then we shall allow this document to be used in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, we have up on the screen 6D736, which purports to be a post-combat report of the 243rd Brigade, your brigade. The date, as we can see, is the 13th of April, 1999, and if we can scroll down to the bottom I would ask you to identify the stamp and the signature. Is this in fact another combat report signed by your Chief of Staff, Dragan Kolundzija with your seal which I presume from--

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's one of the documents signed by the Chief of Staff, Dragan Kolundzija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can look at section 1.2, there we go, we see that the report covers -- well, just so there's no confusion based on my poor Serbian, could we have 1.2 read by you, sir, so we can see what geographic region and what specific events this combat report relates to.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the decision of the 12th of April, 1999, a blockade was carried out in coordinated action of the company of PJP Urosevac, the routing and destruction of the Siptar terrorist forces in the sectors of Firaja, Brod, and Slatina. The effects of the action: 15 [as interpreted] terrorists were liquidated."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I perhaps by speaking earlier had caused an error to come in the transcript. I think the witness testified, in fact, the document lists 14 terrorists, so the transcript at page 36 line 9 ought to reflect 14 terrorists. Now, General, this combat report of your brigade, first of all, do you have recollection of reporting about the actions undertaken on the 12th and 13th of April by your forces and by the "ceta" of the PJP Urosevac; that is to say, does this document refresh your recollection of the same?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we reported to the Pristina Corps command about the fact that we had carried out a blockade. The route from Duganovici to Strpce was cut off and the road was blocked to the right and to the left of that very road, and that road became again passable, the road to Strpce and further on to Prizren because the terrorist forces had been routed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it references here an order -- pardon me, an "odluka," which would be on a decision of the 12th of April, 1999. Whose decision is being referenced and what kind of decision are we talking about? Are we talking about a written decision, an "odluka" map, a decision map, or both?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every decision must contain a map and a written part, but a decision may be communicated orally, too. In this case I assume, based on my recollection, that was a written decision to the effect that in this sector, the area where the road was, that the terrorist forces should be routed along this road in concerted action with the PJP forces to secure it. And as far as I can remember, we provided support, mortar support, or rather, that was a mortar battery or a mortar company, it depends on the terminology. We used the terminology "company," but elsewhere it's called battery, a mortar battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this decision, who would have authorised or issued the decision for this action to take place to involve the mortar battery or company of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade and the "ceta" of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, no motorised companies were used. A mortar company was used. There is a very big difference. And now, as for the decision to use my unit, any element thereof, this decision is made by me, the brigade commander, or in my absence the Chief of Staff of the brigade. And as for the MUP, that would be their staff chief according to their chain of command. And since this was to be a joint action, since the route had to be cleared, made passable, for the traffic of civilians, MUP, and the army, it was a concerted action, it was a joint action, launched to rout those terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I take it then, now that your recollection has been refreshed, you are withdrawing your testimony of the other day at transcript page 18917, lines 1 through 7, that this was solely a MUP action in the region of Slatina, April the 13th, 1999? Do you stand corrected now today?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I maintain what I said, a joint action in our language has several meanings. If you say "joint" and if MUP is the mainstay of the combat action, they move forward; and if I provide mortar support, then this is a joint action. But the mainstay of this action is the force that is in direct contact with the enemy. This is how it is envisaged in the Rules of Combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the "odluka," or decision, that you would have prepared or your Chief of Staff, for your forces, as you indicated, would have been reduced to a map - isn't that correct - with identifying both the location and the assignments of the VJ component involved in this joint action as well as the MUP of the Republic of Serbia component involved in this joint action. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision contains the basic elements of both forces and of -- both sides and the third side, the enemy, but that's based on the assessment. The enemy forces are listed on the basis of the intelligence data at our disposal. The decision is the initial document for the performance of a combat action, and in the course of the actual engagement the decision is amended depending on the actual developments on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, General, if such a decision or order is to be amended on the terrain in the course of engagement, based on actual developments, am I correct that only you as the commander who initially approved the decision, only you could change it; that is to say, your subordinate units or the MUP units in the field could not change your decision?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now we go back to the previous question, or rather, the questions in the last session. The decision is the initial document, and in the course of an engagement the commander carrying out that part of the combat action is entitled to amend the decision because the situation dictates it. In this case you can see that this was signed by the brigade Chief of Staff, but regardless of who signed it the situation may dictate that the decision be amended. The decision about the police is not made by me, but by their superior, that would be the MUP staff, or rather, the MUP in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now you've mentioned the MUP staff in Pristina for the first time. You were talking about Urosevac and Kacanik. How many personnel from MUP were you in contact with in planning the action and preparing the documents with respect to this action?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say that, I mean the MUP in Pristina or the MUP in Urosevac, along their chain of command. I contacted only the chief of the SUP in Urosevac, Bogoljub Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up. Now if we look at the section that you just read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if I can interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You are going to have to start prioritizing what you're doing here. There's a limit to the detail that you can explore unless there are particular reasons for it of every event that the witness has spoken to. So can we have some indication of what's involved in this cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, this was a far-reaching examination in covering Kacanik, Urosevac, and part of Gnjilane, those are three municipalities, and the witness in direct testified to a whole sort of villages, particularly Vata and Slatina where we are at now, I also intend to cover Dubrava and Reka, Stagovo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought we were now in Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are still in Vata and Slatina, Your Honour. Dubrava is coming up shortly in a matter of a question or two. They are close to one another so it does overlap sometimes in direct. The problem we have is the very general nature of the testimony leaves many details -- the testimony in direct leaves many details that I have to flush out to describe the situation in the field so that the wrong inferences are not made and that we don't have a situation where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So how long do you envisage your cross-examination lasting?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I anticipate finishing within this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, you read in here that there were 14 terrorists that were killed. Did any of the reporting from either your VJ units in the field or the MUP units they were supporting mention anything about civilians that were casualties?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, and it says here, it was not mentioned, as far as I can remember. Because we did not carry out the search of the terrain, we did not carry out any on-site investigations, and we were not in contact with those casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And had there been any -- strike that. Had there been any civilian deaths, they would be reported and recorded in your combat reports as part of the normal practice and procedure for such reports. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, yes, but we did not have any contacts with those bodies and I don't recall whether anyone jotted down this information. But at any rate, I do know that these were the figures. It would have been only natural to write that down, but it would have depended on the actual location of those people who were killed, whether they were killed in -- within the battle order, the combat disposition, with the units that were involved in the fighting or whether this was somebody who was just a passer-by, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, do you know whether this information comes from your units who were actually on the ground, first-hand, or if it was reported to you in the regular course of the reporting of the MUP units engaged in this joint, legitimate anti-terrorist action against the terrorist forces in that particular region?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We amended the data, and I can't recall whether I gave the data to MUP or the other way around. But at any rate we exchanged the information, the information that we obtained in the field.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The beginning of the reply should read: "We exchanged information."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to move on to Dubrava and Reka. Now, if we can look at -- no, I think the -- you -- I'm going to try and short-circuit this somewhat, sir. You testified about Dubrava and Reka at several points on Friday. I think we can conclude that the gist of your testimony was that, again in this instance, you claimed that the MUP was doing the action and that the army was merely holding defensive positions. I think that's at pages 18920 through 18921 of the transcript. I'd like to take you through Exhibit 6D1314 in e-court, which I think will be a combat report of the Pristina Corps, strictly confidential number 692-1/61, dated 26 May 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we get a reference. When was this document announced that it would be used in the examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On the addendum from Thursday afternoon. If you see it's the one, two, three, four, fifth from the bottom on that list of documents from the addendum, 6D1314, before the testimony on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yet another document that was announced until -- that was announced at a later stage, and a little while ago my colleague indicated that he would only be using 6D1313.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has it yet to come before us, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe it has, Your Honour. Again, I'm sort of working at a disadvantage, having not drafted the original list, to know whether it was one used with the previous witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, but are you going to be referring to it or is it 6D1314 that you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, 14 and 13, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I stand corrected in that regard. 13 was one I knew for sure was coming up in relation to Belanica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is yet another document that arises, it would appear, from the way in which the examination-in-chief was conducted, and in these circumstances since there's no suggestion it's not relevant and since it will assist in completing the picture, we will allow it to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, first of all, with respect to this document, the section starting in 1.1, and trying to avoid having to have you read the whole thing, I would just ask you if you can look in there and if you can confirm for me that in fact the 243rd mbr of the VJ had combat activities manifested by the STS in the villages of Kovacevac, Nika, Reka, Bicevac, and Dubrava, and if this description encompasses what you understood as the Dubrava and Reka villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm afraid that we will get a completely different interpretation, wrong interpretation of this document, because you don't have the English translation. Perhaps the best way to proceed would be for the witness to read this whole passage that my learned colleague Mr. Ivetic wants to ask about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It doesn't seem to me at first sight that there's anything wrong with that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, please, Mr. Jelic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour. The Siptar terrorist forces manifested activities in the -- that means attacked the brigade units in the sectors of defence, and then you have the villages listed: Kovacevac, Nika, Reka, Bicevac, and Dubrava in the area around Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, if you're unhappy about that then you can deal with the matter in re-examination. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I believe I had said manifested by the STS, but in any event if we can-- I'm just trying to make sure that we're dealing with the right region, that that is Dubrava and Reka, which was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does that zone of defence encompass the villages of Dubrava and Reka in Kacanik municipality?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those villages, all the way up to Urosevac, the whole territory was in the zone of defence of the brigade, but not in the sectors. There is a difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe it will become clear if we look at page 2, 2.1 is the section I want, and you'll see an entry there for the date of the 25th of May, 1999, General, and could you read for us the report segment of this post-combat report for the 25th of May, 1999, it's the one, two, three, fourth bullet point under 2.1, talking about the activities and effects and consequences of the reported activities.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 25th of May, 1999, from 500 hours until 1900 hours, the Dubrava action was executed and part of the forces of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade with MUP forces." That's a document of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe the transcript should reflect Pristina Corps command, but I think it's not that relevant. I agree, General, and would you agree with me that, in fact, you are aware of an action, an anti-terrorist action, a legitimate anti-terrorist action under the name Dubrava conducted by a portion of your forces and forces of the MUP in and around Dubrava and Reka villages conducted --

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
